key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning delivered the most accurate predictions for weld performance metrics, while multitask neural networks provided strong shared-learning generalization across related welding tasks.
engineering_relevance: Reliable prediction of UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness can reduce trial-and-error in welding process design and help improve structural integrity and quality control.
method: Compared multitask neural network (shared hidden layers with task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Predicted three related outputs: UTS, weld bead hardness, and HAZ hardness from a shared dataset.
Evaluated models using RMSE and R² to compare accuracy and generalization.
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved RMSE/R² of 0.0263/0.9863 for UTS, 0.0467/0.9782 for weld hardness, and 0.1109/0.8453 for HAZ hardness, outperforming MTNN on task-specific accuracy.
watch_item: Performance may depend on dataset size and distribution, so the stronger ensemble accuracy may not transfer directly to new welding conditions or unseen materials.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
